source: no published source; read from the installed 2.0.6 build

lines: Three separate oscillators side by side, each with its own tuning and pulse width, and each giving a sine, a triangle, a falling ramp and a square.
Sets that oscillator's pitch over four octaves, -2 to +2; at the middle of its travel the oscillator sounds C4.
Scales that oscillator's Mod input before it is added to the pitch in volts, 0 to 1. It starts at 0, so the jack reaches nothing until this is turned up.
Detunes that oscillator by about half a semitone either way, -1 to +1.
Scales that oscillator's Pwm input before it shifts the pulse width, 0 to 1. It starts at 0, so the jack reaches nothing until this is turned up.
Narrows that oscillator's pulse, 0 to 1. The pulse stays fully open over the bottom half of the travel and only begins to narrow past the middle, closing at the top.
Sets that oscillator's pitch at 1V an octave, added to the Tune knob.
Added to that oscillator's pitch in volts, scaled by the Mod knob; with Mod at 0 nothing here reaches the pitch.
Shifts that oscillator's pulse width, taken between -5V and +5V and scaled by the Pwm knob; with Pwm at 0 nothing here reaches the pulse width.
A sine at that oscillator's pitch, swinging ±5V.
A triangle at that oscillator's pitch, swinging ±5V.
A falling ramp at that oscillator's pitch, swinging ±5V.
A square at that oscillator's pitch, swinging ±5V, its width set by the Pulse knob.
Note — the module prints a line of debugging text for each of its three oscillators on every sample, which fills Rack's log file and costs processor time.
Note — the maker named none of the fifteen knobs and none of the twenty-one jacks, so hovering one shows no name; the panel lettering is the only naming there is.
Note — the three oscillators are wholly separate: nothing on the panel joins one to another.
Note — every jack reads one channel and every output writes one channel.

3mountains.notes: There is no published source and no manual: pluginUrl, manualUrl and sourceUrl are all empty in the installed plugin.json, and the plugin folder holds only the binary and res. Everything here comes from the census positions, the panel art res/3mountainsVCVCompatible2.svg, and a disassembly of the unstripped plugin.dylib. Index order is not panel order anywhere on this module: the first oscillator holds parameters 0 to 4, inputs 0 to 2 and outputs 0 to 3, and the other two are interleaved pairs after them, so for example the four output jacks of the leftmost oscillator run 1, 3, 2, 0 from left to right. tripleOSC::step calls printf("sine pulsewidth with CV %f\n", ...) unconditionally once per oscillator per sample, inside the audio loop. The Pulse knob computes its width as (0.5 - knob) * about 2.04 + 1 and then clamps to 0 and 1, so the whole bottom half of its travel gives the same fully open pulse, and the configured default of 0 sits inside that dead half. The Mod and Pwm knobs are both configured with a default of 0, which makes the left and right jacks of every oscillator inert on a freshly placed module. The frequency is 130.8Hz raised by the pitch in octaves and then multiplied by one plus two to the power of the Fine knob over twelve, which doubles it: Fine at zero therefore gives 261.6Hz, and the knob's range of -1 to +1 works out at about fifty cents either way. The res folder also holds 3mountains.svg, an older panel whose lettering reads CV, fine, pwm and pulsewidth where the shipped one reads Mod, Fine, Pwm and Pulse; the binary loads the shipped one.
